text:
Passive movements are motions of a joint or limb produced entirely by an external force, such as a therapist or equipment, while the person’s muscles remain relaxed and do not actively contract. They are used to maintain joint range of motion, prevent stiffness, and assess joint integrity when active movement is not possible or advisable. Historically, they were also described in ancient Greek gymnastics and used mainly to train athletes for competition.
